dedupe_keys.name: concawe performance of european cross country oil pipelines spillage statistics since 1971

description: Concawe collects spillage data on European cross-country oil pipelines each year and publishes a statistical summary report. Report 6/23 (May 2023) covers 2021 and the full history since 1971: at over 35,000 km the surveyed inventory includes most such pipelines in Europe, carrying some 650 million cubic metres a year of crude oil and products. Performance is analysed by gross and net spill volumes and by causes grouped as mechanical failure, operational, corrosion, natural hazard and third party, including theft, together with the inventory's length, diameter and age distribution, throughput, fatalities, injuries, fires and the use of in-line inspection tools. In 2021 four spills were reported, two of them theft-related; the other two gave 0.06 spills per 1,000 km against a long-term average of 0.43. Coverage is continental. The reports are free PDF downloads, and reproduction is permitted with acknowledgement. Caveats: the data are aggregate tables in reports, not a database of events, and reporting relies on operators taking part. They support failure-rate priors for hazard exposure, fragility and cascading failure studies of liquid pipelines, and complement the EGIG gas pipeline incident data and PHMSA incident data catalogued by other pieces, and UKOPA data catalogued here.
